_comment: Project-local checks for the competency tests the shipped registry does not cover. Merged with the installed registry at run time by run_competency_checks.py, so the suite's own 61 checks stay current. Ids follow the suite's <CATEGORY-PREFIX>-<NNN> convention; the number is deliberately the competency-test number, so CMP-019 answers CT-19.

checks.title: Same IRI used for two unrelated concepts
checks.description: One IRI is typed with two classes where neither is a specialisation of the other, so two mappings are minting the same identifier for different things. Distinct from TQL-001, which compares BIND expressions in query text: this asks the question of the real output, where a collision built from differently-named columns still shows up.
checks.remediation: Decide which concept owns the IRI template and change the other mapping's BIND, or add the discriminator (an entity-type token, a source-system prefix) that keeps the two apart.
checks.cucumber_scenario: No IRI denotes two unrelated concepts

checks.title: Locally defined class has no place in the class hierarchy
checks.description: A class declared in a namespace this project owns has neither rdfs:subClassOf nor owl:equivalentClass, so it hangs outside the hierarchy entirely. Stricter than STR-004, which is satisfied by any defining axiom including owl:disjointWith: a class can be formally constrained and still be unreachable by any hierarchy traversal. Imported vocabularies are excluded by namespace.
checks.remediation: Give the class a superclass, or an equivalentClass axiom that places it. If it is genuinely a top-level concept, say so explicitly with rdfs:subClassOf owl:Thing.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every locally defined class is placed in the hierarchy

checks.title: Label or definition minted by the transformation
checks.description: A CONSTRUCT template attaches skos:prefLabel, skos:altLabel or skos:definition to a term that is not a per-row instance -- a class, property or controlled-vocabulary member the model owns. Two artefacts then state the same term's label and nothing keeps them in step. Run against the sketch graph, where per-row entities are recognisable by the sketch's own scratch namespace.
checks.remediation: Move the label or definition into the ontology or taxonomy that declares the term, and drop the triple from the mapping.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Term metadata is stated only by the artefact that declares the term

checks.title: Declared property never used in the resulting graph
checks.description: An owl:ObjectProperty or owl:DatatypeProperty is declared in the ontology but appears as a predicate nowhere in the output. The property half of CNF-005, which asks the same question about classes. Info rather than Warning because a property outside a given batch's scope is legitimately unused.
checks.remediation: Confirm the omission is intentional. If the property should be populated, the mapping for it is missing; if it is obsolete, deprecate or remove it.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every declared property is either used or knowingly unused

checks.title: Generated entity missing a required object property
checks.description: An entity of a class the project's graph pattern governs has none of the object-property links that pattern requires. Typically an empty source cell: the row still produces the entity, and only the one link silently disappears. The required (class, property) pairs are a VALUES table in the check, which is where a project states its own rule.
checks.remediation: Trace the row back to source. If the source value is genuinely absent, decide whether the entity should be produced at all; if it is present, the BIND that builds the link is failing.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every generated entity carries the object properties its pattern requires

checks.title: Generated graph uses an unexpected modelling pattern
checks.description: An entity carries gist:numericValue directly instead of via a gist:Magnitude node. The output is syntactically fine and every triple parses; the number simply has nowhere to carry its unit or quantity kind, so it cannot be compared or converted.
checks.remediation: Rewrite the mapping to build a magnitude node between the entity and its number, and attach the unit to that node.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Quantities follow the agreed magnitude pattern

checks.title: Magnitude missing a numeric value
checks.description: An instance of gist:Magnitude, or any subclass, has no gist:numericValue. DAT-004 asks the same question about the unit; a magnitude needs both to be a quantity at all. Usually an empty source cell that still built the magnitude node, so the defect is invisible in the row count.
checks.remediation: Guard the magnitude node's construction on the value being present, or supply the missing source value.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every magnitude carries its numeric value

checks.title: Unit of measure incompatible with the quantity
checks.description: A magnitude is measured in a unit that cannot express its quantity kind -- a pressure in litres, a length in seconds. DAT-004 confirms a unit is present and is a gist:UnitOfMeasure; this asks whether it is the right kind of unit. The allowed (magnitude class, unit) pairs are a VALUES table in the check; a class not named there is not governed.
checks.remediation: Correct the unit in the mapping. If the unit is right and the quantity kind is wrong, the magnitude's class is what needs changing.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every magnitude's unit can express its quantity

checks.title: Instance IRI built under a superseded base
checks.description: A BIND still CONCATs instance IRIs under the base agreed for a class that has since been replaced -- typically because the concept moved into a shared or core namespace and took its agreed IRI pattern with it. Distinct from CNF-001/CNF-002, which ask whether the class and property IRIs a mapping names are declared: those terms can all be correct while every instance the mapping mints still lands under the old base.
checks.remediation: Update the mapping's BIND to the pattern the superseding class declares, and decide what happens to the identifiers already issued -- re-minting them changes the identity of every entity downstream, so a migration usually needs owl:sameAs or a rewrite of the existing graph.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Instance IRIs follow the pattern the current model agrees on

checks.metric: business key uniqueness within an output
checks.title: Two entities share a business key
checks.description: Two instances of one class carry the same value for the property the project treats as that class's business key, so one real-world thing has been created twice under two identifiers. The mirror of CMP-002 (one IRI for two things) and not DAT-003, which is one subject repeating a value rather than two subjects sharing one.
checks.remediation: Decide which identifier survives, merge the two entities, and give the source a uniqueness constraint on that key -- or, if the key is legitimately non-unique, stop treating it as an identifier.
checks.cucumber_scenario: A business key identifies at most one entity

checks.title: Single-valued relationship carries two values
checks.description: An entity carries two values for a relationship the agreed graph pattern allows one of, typically because two mappings each contribute a link and disagree. Reported by a project check rather than by LOG-002 because the ontology does not declare the property owl:FunctionalProperty -- the cardinality is agreed in the mapping specification and never written into the TBox.
checks.remediation: Establish which source is authoritative for the link and drop the other mapping's triple; if both are legitimate, the property is not single-valued and the agreed pattern needs changing. Declaring it owl:FunctionalProperty afterwards moves the check to LOG-002.
checks.cucumber_scenario: A single-valued relationship has one value

checks.title: Template asserts a property outside its declared domain
checks.description: A CONSTRUCT template hangs a property off an entity whose class is not the property's rdfs:domain, nor a subclass of it. The suite reports the same condition as CNF-003, but of real output -- after the CSVs are read and the mappings run. Everything needed to know it earlier is in the query text, and a mapping wired to no CSV yet is never reported at all.
checks.remediation: Use the property the class actually has, or type the entity as the class the property expects. If both are right, the ontology's domain is wrong and should be widened.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every property a template asserts belongs to the class it is asserted on

checks.metric: deprecated term still built by a transformation
checks.title: Mapping still builds a deprecated term
checks.description: A mapping constructs a class or property the model marks owl:deprecated. QUA-003 asks this of an ontology and of data; neither reaches the mappings, which are where the use originates -- the data is deprecated because the transformation that made it is.
checks.remediation: Move the mapping to the replacement the ontology names, then decide what happens to the data already built with the old term.
checks.cucumber_scenario: No mapping builds a term the model has deprecated

checks.title: One class built with different shapes by different mappings
checks.description: Two or more mappings build instances of the same class with different property sets, so the shape of an entity depends on which file made it. Invisible per file: each mapping builds a reasonable entity and only the union is lopsided.
checks.remediation: Decide which properties every instance of the class must carry, and either add them to the thinner mapping or split the class so the two populations are honestly different.
checks.cucumber_scenario: A class has one shape however it was built

checks.title: One predicate filled with different datatypes by different mappings
checks.description: The value of one predicate is typed in one mapping and left untyped, or typed differently, in another. Values of a single property that will not compare, sort or aggregate against each other, with no individual file looking wrong.
checks.remediation: Type the value the same way in every mapping, at the datatype the property's rdfs:range declares.
checks.cucumber_scenario: A predicate carries one datatype across the mapping set

checks.title: Mapping builds a term outside the ontology's import closure
checks.description: A term the mappings build is declared in a file passed on the command line but is not reachable from the integration ontology through owl:imports. The checks pass because of how they were invoked rather than because the ontology is complete, and the first consumer to load the ontology as published gets neither the term nor a warning.
checks.remediation: Give the vocabulary an ontology IRI and import it, or state plainly that it is an external dependency the consumer must supply.
checks.cucumber_scenario: Every term a mapping builds is reachable through owl:imports

checks.title: One prefix bound to two namespaces across the mapping set
checks.description: Two mappings bind the same prefix to different namespaces. Each file is internally consistent, so no per-file check fires; downstream the term-level checks report an undeclared term, which names the symptom in one file rather than the disagreement between two. The hash-versus-slash slip on an external vocabulary is the everyday form.
checks.remediation: Agree one namespace per prefix across the mapping set, preferably in a shared PREFIX header the queries include rather than repeat.
checks.cucumber_scenario: A prefix means the same thing in every mapping

checks.metric: output stability across a model change
checks.title: Triplified output differs from the agreed golden copy
checks.description: The mapping set no longer produces triples a stored golden copy records, or now produces triples it does not. The review aids compare two outputs; this compares the current run against what was agreed, which is the comparison a reviewer wants at a version bump -- 'the ontology moved and the tests still pass' becomes a list of what moved with it.
checks.remediation: Review each difference and either fix the mapping or update the golden deliberately, in the same commit as the change that justifies it.
checks.cucumber_scenario: The output changes only where a change was intended
